name: Ampero Mini model library
about: Model names and the codes the pedal stores for them, for the Hotone Ampero Mini (firmware V2.2). Unofficial, not affiliated with Hotone. Third-party brand names are used only to say what a model is based on.

status_values.pedal-proven: code was set on a real pedal and read back from the preset record
status_values.scroll-derived: code seen while scrolling the pedal's list (FX2); not read back
status_values.list-order: code follows from the list order and a rule that held at the proven points; not checked
status_values.code-unknown: model name known from the editor, code not read yet

fields.screen: 1-based position in the editor's list for this block
fields.code: value stored in the record for this model (null = unknown)
fields.id: number in the manufacturer's effect list (null = not in that list)
fields.firmware_added: in the editor's list but not in the manufacturer's effect list
fields.based_on: real-world equivalent as listed by the manufacturer (null if none listed or unknown)
fields.based_on_status: listed | none-listed (original model) | unknown (not in the manufacturer's list)
fields.renamed: note where the editor's name differs from the manufacturer's list
fields.notes: AMP only. tone, known_for and tip are written by the project in its own words about the real-world amp; null where the amp is not confidently identified. General background, not measurements.

notes: FX1, FX2 and FX3 share many names but store different codes. Always use the code for the slot you are writing.
Only pedal-proven codes should be sent to a pedal without a read-back.

notes.tone: Warm, thick and a little compressed. Small amp, so it gets gritty early.
notes.known_for: Early rock and roll, blues and roots music.
notes.tip: Rolling the guitar volume back cleans it up. Good with a light drive in front.

notes.tone: Round, full and punchy. Stays fairly clean at low gain, then turns gritty and fat when pushed.
notes.known_for: Blues and rock and roll. Many later guitar amps grew out of this design.
notes.tip: Works best with single coils. Pairs well with an overdrive for more sustain.

notes.tone: Very clean, big and sparkly, with lots of headroom and a chimey top end.
notes.known_for: Country, surf, jazz and clean pop. A common base for pedals.
notes.tip: Takes pedals very well. Do not expect natural breakup at normal volumes.

notes.tone: Bright, chimey and mid-forward British clean to light crunch. The normal channel is the softer, rounder one.
notes.known_for: Jangly British pop and rock. Brian May and the Beatles are the usual names.
notes.tip: Breaks up nicely when pushed. Try Top Boost (next entry) if it is too soft.

models.name: Jazz Clean
models.based_on: legendary Jazz Chorus solid state combo

notes.tone: Glassy, very clean solid-state sound with a wide built-in chorus.
notes.known_for: 80s clean tones, new wave and indie.
notes.tip: No tube-style breakup, so lean on pedals for drive. Easy to play with delay and reverb.

notes.tone: Chimey clean in the British Class A style, with a fuller low end than a plain AC30.
notes.tip: Use it for clean parts that need some body.

notes.tone: Rich boutique clean with a bit of shimmer.
notes.tip: A step toward polite and polished, rather than raw.

notes.tone: Clean to light break-up with a sweet, open top end.
notes.tip: A good platform for pedals.

notes.tone: Same amp as Baseman Norm, bright channel: more sparkle and edge, less body.
notes.tip: Pick this over Norm when your guitar sounds dull or dark.

notes.tone: Brighter and punchier than the normal channel, with more chime and bite.
notes.tip: Good for crunch with a bit of treble boost in front.

notes.tone: The dirty side of the same amp: a chimey, touch-sensitive crunch.
notes.known_for: Classic rock rhythm and bluesy leads.
notes.tip: Dynamic. Pick harder for more grit.

notes.tone: Mid-gain, smooth rock overdrive from the second channel.
notes.tip: Sits well with a booster in front for solos.

notes.tone: Warm, thick, a bit loose, and bluesy. Less gain than later Marshalls.
notes.known_for: The roots of British rock and blues.
notes.tip: Needs a boost or gain pedal for harder rock.

notes.tone: The pedal's own take on the same Marshall amp as the entry before it.
notes.tip: Compare by ear with the entry before it.

notes.tone: Like the base entry with both inputs linked, which gives more gain and body.
notes.tip: Try it when the base entry is too polite.

notes.tone: Classic Plexi-style crunch: open, loud, and punchy.
notes.tip: Takes a booster very well. Great with humbuckers or single coils.

notes.tone: The pedal's own take on the same Marshall amp as the entry before it.
notes.tip: Compare by ear with the entry before it.

notes.tone: Like the base entry with the channels linked: more gain and fatter lows.
notes.tip: Use it when you want a bit more drive without a pedal.

models.name: Hot Kitty Drive
models.based_on: Bad Cat Hot Cat 30 drive channel

notes.tone: Rich, touch-sensitive overdrive with a hint of both Vox and Marshall.
notes.tip: Responds well to guitar volume.

models.name: Messe IIC+ 1
models.based_on: Mesa/Boogie Mark II C+ Lead - switch combo 1

notes.tone: Smooth, saturated and singing lead tone with a tight low end.
notes.known_for: Lead playing in rock and fusion. Carlos Santana is closely linked to early Mesa amps.
notes.tip: The three entries are different switch settings. A/B them for taste.

models.name: Messe IIC+ 2
models.based_on: Mesa/Boogie Mark II C+ Lead - switch combo 2

notes.tone: Another switch setting of the same Mark II C+ lead voice.
notes.known_for: Lead playing in rock and fusion.
notes.tip: A/B with the other two entries (22 to 24).

models.name: Messe IIC+ 3
models.based_on: Mesa/Boogie Mark II C+ Lead - switch combo 3

notes.tone: Another switch setting of the same Mark II C+ lead voice.
notes.known_for: Lead playing in rock and fusion.
notes.tip: A/B with the other two entries (22 to 24).

notes.tone: Crunchy high-gain tone, tight and punchy.
notes.tip: A good rhythm pick before the lead channel.

notes.tone: Mid-heavy, punchy 80s hard rock crunch.
notes.known_for: Hard rock and metal. A staple with a boost in front.
notes.tip: Takes an overdrive pedal in front very well.

notes.tone: Modern high-gain with a Marshall-like voice, tight and aggressive.
notes.tip: Good for rhythm and lead.

notes.tone: A second version of the same Brown Eye voice.
notes.tip: Compare it with the entry before it.

notes.tone: Smooth, harmonically rich crunch to lead gain.
notes.tip: Good all-rounder when you want gain that stays clear.

notes.tone: Tight, compressed and saturated 90s gain.
notes.tip: More compression than the 800. Watch for a fizzy top end on bright guitars.

notes.tone: Aggressive modern high gain with a tight, controlled low end and a lot of drive.
notes.tip: Two versions exist (blue and silver) and the + entries are the pedal's own take. Compare by ear.

notes.tone: Aggressive modern high gain with a tight, controlled low end and a lot of drive.

models.name: Engle Saga 1
models.based_on: ENGL Savage 120 E610 CH4 contour off

notes.tone: Tight, aggressive modern metal gain with a big low end.
notes.tip: The contour setting changes the mid shape. Listen to both entries to pick.

notes.tone: Tight, aggressive modern metal gain with a big low end.
notes.tip: The contour setting changes the mid shape. Listen to both entries to pick.

notes.tone: Hotter version of the same amp family: more gain and saturation.
notes.tip: Use it when you need extra gain without a pedal.

notes.tone: A second version of the same Brown Eye voice.
notes.tip: Compare it with the entry before it.

notes.tone: Aggressive, tight and saturated lead channel.
notes.known_for: Metal and hard rock, with ties to Van Halen era rock.
notes.tip: Very high gain, so keep the guitar volume up and use the noise gate.

notes.tone: Thick, saturated lead tone with long sustain.
notes.tip: Tight low end, so it handles fast riffs.

notes.tone: Polished, saturated lead with a tight low end.
notes.tip: Three entries are different switch settings. A/B them.

notes.tone: Polished, saturated lead with a tight low end.

notes.tone: Thick, mid-forward high gain with a heavy low end.
notes.tip: Good for slow, heavy riffs.

models.name: Rector Dual V
models.based_on: Mesa/Boogie Dual Rectifier CH3 vintage mode

notes.tone: Massive, tight and heavy. Vintage mode is looser and spongier.
notes.tip: Pair with a tight cab. Both modes are worth trying.

models.name: Rector Dual M
models.based_on: Mesa/Boogie Dual Rectifier CH3 modern mode

notes.tone: Massive, tight and heavy. Modern mode is tighter and louder.
notes.tip: Pair with a tight cab. Both modes are worth trying.

notes.tone: Aggressive modern high gain with a tight, controlled low end and a lot of drive.
notes.tip: Two versions exist (blue and silver) and the + entries are the pedal's own take. Compare by ear.

notes.tone: Dense, modern high gain with a firm low end.
notes.tip: The editor calls it Blue M but the manufacturer's list says Red M. Listen before relying on the name.

notes.tone: Clear, articulate bass preamp with a hi-fi tone.
notes.tip: Good for DI-style bass or when you want a clean, detailed sound.

notes.tone: Punchy, warm and big at the low end.
notes.tip: Reliable for rock bass.

models.name: Ampage Flip
models.based_on: Ampeg B-15 Flip Top bass amp

notes.tone: Round, warm and thumpy vintage bass tone.
notes.known_for: Classic soul and studio bass. James Jamerson is the well-known user.
notes.tip: Great with flatwound strings.

notes.tone: Vintage 60s-style bass tone, clean and round.
notes.tip: Use it for a vintage, rounded sound.

notes.tone: Punchy, tight and articulate with plenty of low-mid push.
notes.tip: Cuts through a mix well.

models.name: Acoustic Preamp 2
models.based_on: AER Colourizer 2 acoustic preamp with EQ

notes.tone: Clear, natural acoustic guitar preamp with tone shaping.
notes.known_for: Acoustic guitar and pickup-equipped acoustic instruments.
notes.tip: Good for acoustic guitars with a piezo pickup.
